title: An element lifting (1,0) in a finite algebra is a root of a monic polynomial reducing to (x-1)x^d
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal contained in the Jacobson radical of $A$ (the intersection of all maximal ideals of $A$), and $A\to B$ a finite ring map ($B$ is a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]). Suppose that $B/IB=B_1\times B_2$ is a product of $A/I$-algebras such that the structure map $A/I\to B_1$ is surjective, and let $b\in B$ be an element whose image in $B/IB$ is $(1,0)$. Then there are an integer $d\ge1$ and a monic polynomial $f\in A[x]$ with $f(b)=0$ in $B$ and $f\equiv(x-1)x^d$ modulo $I$; equivalently $f=x^d(x-1)+a_dx^d+\dots+a_1x+a_0$ with $a_0,\dots,a_d\in I$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0EM0 (lemma-helper-finite, line 2290) and its proof (uses Lemma 07M4 lemma-lift-idempotent-upstairs, Nakayama Algebra Lemma 00DV lemma-NAK, Algebra Lemma 00H5 lemma-integral-integral-over-ideal, and faithful flatness of the etale A -> A' whose image contains V(I): Algebra Lemma 05CK lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective, Proposition 00I1 proposition-fppf-open); Stacks writes the hypothesis as 'A/I -> B_1/IB_1 surjective', where B_1 is already an A/I-algebra, so B_1/IB_1 = B_1

proof.text: *Lifting the idempotent.* Write $\bar e=(1,0)\in B/IB=B_1\times B_2$, an idempotent, which is the image of $b$. Since $B$ is a finitely generated $A$-module, $B$ is integral over $A$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]. By [lem-weil-pbc-lift-idempotent-upstairs] there are a ring map $A\to A'$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ etale such that $\alpha:A/I\to A'/IA'$ is an isomorphism, and an idempotent $e'\in B':=B\otimes_AA'$ whose image under $B'\to B'/IB'=B\otimes_A(A'/IA')\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}\otimes\alpha^{-1}}B\otimes_A(A/I)=B/IB$ is $\bar e$.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 0EM0 (lemma-helper-finite, line 2290), first sentence (Lemma 07M4)

proof.text: *The decomposition upstairs.* $B'$ is a finitely generated $A'$-module (if $b_1,\dots,b_n$ generate $B$ over $A$, the $b_k\otimes1$ generate $B'$ over $A'$). Put $B'_1=B'/(1-e')B'$ and $B'_2=B'/e'B'$; since $e'$ is idempotent, $B'\to B'_1\times B'_2$ is an isomorphism of $A'$-algebras, and both factors are finitely generated $A'$-modules. Reducing modulo $I$ and using the identification $B'/IB'\cong B/IB$ of step 1, under which $e'\mapsto\bar e=(1,0)$, we get $B'_1/IB'_1\cong(B/IB)/(1-\bar e)=B_1$ and $B'_2/IB'_2\cong(B/IB)/\bar e=B_2$, compatibly with the structure maps from $A'/IA'\cong A/I$. In particular the image $b'=(b'_1,b'_2)$ of $b$ in $B'$ satisfies $b'_1\equiv1$ modulo $IB'_1$ and $b'_2\in IB'_2$.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 0EM0 (lemma-helper-finite, line 2290), 'Consider the corresponding A'-algebra decomposition B' = B'_1 x B'_2 which is compatible with the one given in the lemma upon reduction modulo I'

proof.text: *Nakayama.* Let $C$ be the cokernel of the $A'$-linear map $A'\to B'_1$; it is a finitely generated $A'$-module (a quotient of $B'_1$). Since $C/IC$ is the cokernel of $A'/IA'\to B'_1/IB'_1$, which by step 2 is the cokernel of the surjection $A/I\to B_1$, we have $C=(IA')C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-one-plus-ideal-annihilator] (applied to the ring $A'$ and the ideal $IA'$) there is $g\in A'$ with $g-1\in IA'$ and $gC=0$, i.e. $gy$ lies in the image of $A'$ for every $y\in B'_1$.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 0EM0 (lemma-helper-finite, line 2290), 'The map A' -> B'_1 is surjective modulo IA'. By Nakayama's lemma (Algebra, Lemma 00DV) we can find i in IA' such that ...'

proof.text: *Replacing $A'$ by $A'':=A'_g$.* (a) $A\to A''$ is flat: $A\to A'$ is flat because it is etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat], $A'\to A'_g$ is flat as a localization [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat], and a composite of flat ring maps is flat [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-comp]. (b) $A/I\to A''/IA''$ is an isomorphism: $A''/IA''=(A'/IA')_{\bar g}$ and $\bar g=1$ in $A'/IA'$, so $A'/IA'\to A''/IA''$ is an isomorphism, and we compose with $\alpha$. (c) Put $B''=B\otimes_AA''=B'\otimes_{A'}A''=B'_g$ and $B''_k=(B'_k)_g$, so $B''=B''_1\times B''_2$ as $A''$-algebras, each $B''_k$ is a finitely generated $A''$-module, and $B''_k/IB''_k\cong B'_k/IB'_k$ (again because $g\equiv1$ modulo $IA'$). The map $A''\to B''_1$ is surjective: an element $y/g^n$ of $(B'_1)_g$ equals $(gy)/g^{n+1}$, and $gy$ is the image of some $a\in A'$ by step 3, so $y/g^n$ is the image of $a/g^{n+1}$. (d) By step 2 the image $b''=(b''_1,b''_2)$ of $b$ in $B''$ satisfies $b''_1-1\in IB''_1$ and $b''_2\in IB''_2$.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 0EM0 (lemma-helper-finite, line 2290), 'after replacing A' by A'_{1+i} the map A' -> B'_1 is surjective'; 'The map A -> A' [is] flat because it is etale (Algebra, Lemma 00U2)'

proof.text: *The first component.* Since $A''\to B''_1$ is surjective, $IB''_1$ is the image of $IA''$; so there is $a'\in IA''$ mapping to $b''_1-1$, i.e. $b''_1-1-a'=0$ in $B''_1$.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 0EM0 (lemma-helper-finite, line 2290), 'Thus we may pick a' in IA' mapping to b'_1 - 1'

proof.text: *The second component.* $B''_2$ is a finitely generated $A''$-module, hence integral over $A''$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], and $b''_2\in IB''_2=(IA'')B''_2$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-extended-ideal-element-monic] (Algebra, Lemma 00H5, applied to $A''\to B''_2$ and the ideal $IA''$) there is a monic $g_2=x^e+\sum_{j<e}c_jx^j\in A''[x]$ with all $c_j\in IA''$ and $g_2(b''_2)=0$. Put $d=e+1$ and $G=xg_2=x^d+\sum_{j<d}c'_jx^j$ (so $c'_0=0$, $c'_j=c_{j-1}$); then $d\ge1$, all $c'_j\in IA''$ and $G(b''_2)=0$. (Stacks takes $g$ of degree $d$ directly; multiplying by $x$ ensures $d\ge1$, which fails for $g_2$ only when $e=0$, i.e. $B''_2=0$.)

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 0EM0 (lemma-helper-finite, line 2290), 'By Algebra, Lemma 00H5 there exist a monic polynomial g(x) = x^d + sum a'_j x^j of degree d with a'_j in IA' such that g(b'_2) = 0'

proof.text: *A relation in $B''$.* Let $H=(x-1-a')G\in A''[x]$. Its value at $b''=(b''_1,b''_2)$ is computed componentwise: the first factor vanishes at $b''_1$ (step 5) and $G$ vanishes at $b''_2$ (step 6), so $H(b'')=0$. Moreover $H-(x-1)x^d=(x-1)(G-x^d)-a'G$ has degree $\le d$ and all its coefficients in $IA''$ (as $G-x^d$ has coefficients in $IA''$ and $a'\in IA''$). Hence $(b''-1)(b'')^d\in N'':=\sum_{j=0}^dIA''\cdot(b'')^j\subseteq B''$.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 0EM0 (lemma-helper-finite, line 2290), 'Thus the image b' = (b'_1, b'_2) in B' of b is a root of the polynomial (x - 1 - a')g(x). We conclude that (b' - 1)(b')^d in sum IA' (b')^j'

proof.text: *$A\to A''$ is faithfully flat.* Let $\mathfrak m\subset A$ be a maximal ideal. As $I$ lies in the Jacobson radical, $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$, so by step 4(b) $A''/\mathfrak mA''\cong(A''/IA'')/\mathfrak m(A''/IA'')\cong(A/I)/(\mathfrak m/I)=A/\mathfrak m\neq0$. Since $A\to A''$ is flat (step 4(a)), it is faithfully flat [lem-weil-pbc-flat-faithfully-flat-maximal-ideals]. (Stacks argues that the image of $\operatorname{Spec}A''\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is open (Proposition 00I1) and contains $V(I)$, hence every maximal ideal, hence is everything; the fact used is the same, that every maximal ideal of $A$ lies in $V(I)$ and is in the image, and the criterion Algebra Lemma 00HP makes the openness unnecessary.)

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 0EM0 (lemma-helper-finite, line 2290), 'For this it is enough to see that the ring map A -> A' is faithfully flat ... the image contains V(I). Since I is contained in the Jacobson radical of A we conclude'

proof.text: *Descending the relation.* Let $N=\sum_{j=0}^dI\cdot b^j\subseteq B$ (an $A$-submodule) and $M=B/N$. By right exactness of $-\otimes_AA''$, $M\otimes_AA''=B''/N'$ where $N'$ is the image of $N\otimes_AA''$, i.e. the $A''$-submodule generated by the $ib^j\otimes1$ $(i\in I)$, which is $N''$ of step 7. The class of $(b-1)b^d$ in $M$ maps to the class of $(b''-1)(b'')^d$ in $B''/N''$, which is $0$ by step 7. Since $A\to A''$ is faithfully flat (step 8), $M\to M\otimes_AA''$ is injective [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective]; so $(b-1)b^d\in N$, i.e. $(b-1)b^d=\sum_{j=0}^di_jb^j$ with $i_j\in I$.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 0EM0 (lemma-helper-finite, line 2290), 'the condition is that the image of (b - 1)b^d is zero in B/sum Ib^j (use Algebra, Lemma 05CK)'

proof.text: *Conclusion.* Put $f=x^d(x-1)-\sum_{j=0}^di_jx^j\in A[x]$. It is monic of degree $d+1$, $f(b)=0$ by step 9, $d\ge1$ by step 6, and $f\equiv(x-1)x^d$ modulo $I$, with $a_j=-i_j\in I$ in the notation of the statement.
